items.author: jacobvcreech
items.new_information: Ed25519种子不暴露，可用哈希证明升级迁移

evidence.quote: Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.

Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move
their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.

Adding the technical analysis behind this discussion below. The October 7 snapshot of @OpenAI math results contains 722 manuscripts across 372 result families. We conducted a focused review of 8 selected families (10 manuscripts), not an exhaustive audit. Assuming their stated theorems hold, here is what they claim and what follows for cryptography:

What this means for Bitcoin and Ethereum: The reviewed manuscripts do not provide a practical way to recover a wallet’s private key from its public key. If such a method were found for secp256k1—the curve used by Bitcoin and Ethereum accounts—an attacker could forge ECDSA and Schnorr signatures and potentially spend funds wherever the exposed key and

narrower route: recovering KZG’s secret setup value, τ, would enable false proofs under that setup, without recovering validator keys. The reviewed results demonstrate neither attack; any network-level consequences would depend on the attack’s scope and the protocol.

How much cheaper have these results made an attack? We found no demonstrated reduction in the total work needed to break these targets. For secp256k1, a representative generic classical attack takes roughly 2^128 group operations. None of the reviewed results establishes a reduction to 2^100 or 2^80—or another lower end-to-end estimate. Some results improve
theoretical guarantees or asymptotic bounds, but none of the reviewed results demonstrates a cheaper complete attack on these targets. BLS and KZG require separate, attack-specific estimates.

evidence.quote: Another fun fact: if AI breaks any piece of cryptography, its probably hashes before Eliptic curves or RSA.

Hashes are the black magic of cryptography. They take an arbitrary file/string and produce a collision-resistant fingerprint. We’ve had human-powered breaks of deployed hashes. MD2, MD5, SHA-1 have all been broken and protocols upgraded as we became less confident in those hashes. A break of SHA-256, SHA-3, or (for cryptocurrency)  especially Poseidon
wouldn’t be insanely out there.

Of course, this doesn’t matter much. In fact, if either elliptic curves or hashes were broken, most things you actually use, including applications using Groth16 or STARKs in cryptocurrency land, would have real problems.  All most all applications in cryptocurrency and of zk proofs, depend on both assumptions, even if the proof itself does not.

items.summary: Excellion称，Blockstream哈希签名SHRINCS已在Liquid运行并有比特币草案BIP，可在ECDLP被破时替换ECDSA/Schnorr，代价是签名由64字节增至数百字节至数KB。
items.author: Excellion
items.event: 比特币SHRINCS抗破解签名路径
items.new_information: SHRINCS已在Liquid运行并有草案BIP，签名体积变大

evidence.quote: Signatures exist in Minicrypt (the world where one-way functions exist, but public-key encryption does not). Rompel showed in 1990 you can build them from one-way functions alone. The scheme built for this is SHRINCS, from @blksresearch and @n1ckler. It is hash-based, so it does not care about ECDLP, lattices, or any other algebraic assumption. Blockstream

already has it running on @Liquid_BTC via Simplicity, and there is a draft BIP for Bitcoin. Public keys can stay ~32 bytes, so addresses do not have to change. Signatures do. Schnorr is 64 bytes. SHRINCS stateful signatures start around a few hundred bytes if the wallet tracks used keys. The stateless fallback is a few KB.
Blockstream 的研究人员开发了一套叫 SHRINCS 的新签名方案，它只依赖哈希函数，不需要椭圆曲线，也不依赖其他复杂的数学结构。
目前已经在 Liquid 侧链上实现，并且有面向比特币主网的改进提案草案。
现在比特币的 Schnorr 签名只有 64 字节，而 SHRINCS 的签名可能需要几百字节，甚至几 KB。签名越大，一笔交易占用的区块空间就越多，主链每个区块能装的交易就越少，手续费也可能上涨。
